title: Aaryavir Sehwag Debuts, Anvay Dravid Fires as India U-19 Edge Australia by Seven Runs
excerpt: Yashvardhan Chauhan's 54 and 2 for 28 led the way, with debutant Aaryavir Sehwag (28) and Anvay Dravid (38 off 18) starring in a rain-shortened first Youth ODI against Australia at the Niranjan Shah Stadium in Rajkot.
body:
• India Under-19 beat Australia Under-19 by seven runs in the first of three Youth ODIs at the Niranjan Shah Stadium in Rajkot on Friday, a match reduced to 20 overs per side by rain.
  • Yashvardhan Chauhan starred with an all-round show — 54 off 34 balls and 2 for 28 — rescuing India from 88 for 4 with a 69-run fifth-wicket stand alongside Anvay Dravid.
  • Aaryavir Sehwag, son of former opener Virender Sehwag, made his India U-19 debut, opening the innings and scoring 28 off 26 balls with his father watching from the stands.
  • Anvay Dravid, son of former captain Rahul Dravid, smashed 38 off 18 balls at No. 6, striking at 211.11; Mohit Ulva then defended 11 runs in the final over, conceding only three.

Seven-run win caps a rain-hit thriller in Rajkot

India Under-19 opened the three-match Youth ODI series against Australia with a seven-run win in Rajkot on Friday — a rain-shortened 20-over contest at the Niranjan Shah Stadium that stayed alive until the final over, when Mohit Ulva defended 11 runs and conceded only three.

Put in to bat by Australia captain Jack Czosnek, India finished on 182 for 6. Yashvardhan Chauhan anchored the innings with 54 off 34 balls, and Anvay Dravid walked in at No. 6 to blaze 38 off 18 deliveries with two fours and three sixes. Their 69-run stand for the fifth wicket lifted India from 88 for 4 in the 12th over; India plundered 108 runs from their final 10 overs.

Earlier, debutant Aaryavir Sehwag opened the innings — just as his father used to — striking five fours in his 28 off 26 balls and sharing a 45-run stand with captain Lakshya Raichandani, according to The Times of India. Virender Sehwag was in the stands to watch his son's first outing in India colours.

Australia's chase leaned on its captain: Czosnek smashed 55 off 27 balls, Neel Patel made 45 off 31 and Hayden Barbulovic 40 off 24. But Czosnek fell in the 19th over and the chase stalled. Off-spinner Eli Brain was Australia's best bowler with 2 for 29; Chauhan's all-round 54 and 2 for 28 took Player of the Match.

"6 to blaze 38 off 18 deliveries with two fours and three sixes."

Context & Background

The headlines write themselves — a Sehwag opening, a Dravid finishing — but both teenagers earned their Rajkot moment through domestic weight of runs, not surnames.

Aaryavir Sehwag's Cooch Behar Trophy record demanded selection: 297 off 309 balls against Meghalaya in 2024, three short of a triple century, then 496 runs at 70.86 in the 2025 edition, plus standout Delhi Premier League form. Friday was his maiden India U-19 call-up.

Anvay Dravid's rise has been earlier and steeper: captaining Karnataka's U-14s, an unbeaten double century against Tumkur Zone in 2023, top scorer in the 2024 Vijay Merchant Trophy with 459 runs in six matches at 91.80, and 87 off 67 against Sri Lanka U-19 in July. Rajkot was his third India U-19 appearance, following the Youth ODI series in Sri Lanka earlier this year.

The series — Australia Under-19s in India 2026/27 — is part of the long runway to the next ICC U-19 World Cup, where selectors prize temperament under pressure as much as technique. Friday offered both.

Impact & Analysis

India's win said more about depth than star power. At 88 for 4 after 12 overs, the innings could have folded for 140. Instead, Chauhan and Anvay combined timing and brute force to reach a total Australia could not — the middle-order rescue act senior teams value.

With the ball, India's death discipline stood out. Czosnek's dismissal in the 19th over, after three consecutive fours had briefly swung the game, was the decisive blow, and Ulva's final over was a lesson in yorker-length control under pressure.

For Australia, the takeaway is thinner: chasing 183 in a 20-over game, with fifties spread through the innings, should not end seven runs short. Their middle order could not capitalize once Czosnek departed.

Diaspora Angle

For NRI families, this was the most nostalgic U-19 game in years. A generation of diaspora fans grew up watching Virender Sehwag dismantle attacks and Rahul Dravid hold innings together; watching their sons — Aaryavir opening the way his father did, the Dravid name on an Indian scorecard again — collapses two decades of cricket memory into one evening.

What's Next

India take a 1–0 lead into the second of three Youth ODIs, with both teams staying in Rajkot. For Aaryavir Sehwag, the debut was a start, not a statement — he will want a bigger score. For Anvay Dravid, Friday reinforced that his No. 6 finishing role is no accident.
